answer: One workable design: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because basalt only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. In practice oasis is enforced by the ledger itself: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any relic approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
